title.narrative: WFP in Kind Contribution to EA30/2009 South Sudan

description.narrative:
The 9 month proposed programme will provide support to the Diocese of Tombura-Yambio to deliver much needed food, non-food items, water and basic shelter for 5,000 households in 3 Counties of Western Equatoria State.
In Southern Sudan, Western Equatoria State is a relatively fertile environment and is not commonly identified with food insecurity. The productivity of the region has been severely impaired as a direct result of the insecurity posed by the LRA attacks. The ensuing instability and displacement have reduced people’s access to their land and increased pressure on the minimal resources available. Displacement of large numbers of people both internally and from across the Congolese border, will have severe effects on food production and market activities in the affected areas, compounding existing underlying livelihood productivity problems such as access to markets and basic services, lack of agricultural extension services; lack of modern farming skills, limited technical know-how and tools.
The extent of food insecurity recorded in the assessment was significant and widespread with more than 52,000 people reportedly suffering shortages or a complete absence of food. The ability of the host communities to meet the increasing needs of the influx is impossible and the insecurity of the area is reducing productivity while increasing dependency on external supplies. The result is that among the host communities, the food security situation is also in rapid decline.
The WFP in kind contribution will provide food for 5,000 households.
Distribution of rations: In accordance with WFP ration scale, an initial ration of 540g Cereals, Pulses, Vegetable Oil and Iodized Salt will be distributed to IDPs with an additional 80g Sugar and CSB in the 1st 3 months. As recommended by WFP the ration will be reduced to the standard 540g after 5 months. (Refer to table below) This distribution will continue to till the 8th month to reach the July 2010 harvest and ensure seed distributions are effective and minimal seeds are consumed.
Beneficiary Groups Refugees, IDPs First 3 Months Refugees, IDPs Second 5 Months Commodity and Grams/day/person Cereals 450 450 Pulses 50 50 Vegetable Oil 30 30 Iodized Salt 10 10 Sugar 30 Corn Soya Blend 50
Total gr/day 540 + 80 540
Specific attention will be paid to the protection, promotion and support of the care and nutrition of adolescent girls, pregnant mothers, older people, female and child headed households, families with chronically ill members, including people living with HIV/AIDS. Targeted food distributions to 1,000 vulnerable households will continue at the full 540 + 80 ration until the end of the project within which it is anticipated that the general food situation will have improved appreciably.
